title: Case Processing SOP for Lymph Nodes
author: Marda Jorgensen
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bbgnijve
materials: Sample Archiving: a. All materials obtained for this program will be inventoried by the University of Florida Tissue Mapping Center (UF TMC) and archived in the Organ Processing and Pathology Core (OPPC) until use. b. Samples will be released for use or shipped to collaborator(s) upon request by the Principle Investigator.

steps.title: Assign case number
steps.instruction: Assign a case number to each HuBMAP donor tissue using the template YY-001 (two‑digit year, hyphen, sequential three‑digit number starting at 001).

steps.title: Label cassettes, molds, containers
steps.instruction: Generate labels for each cassette, cryomold, and container using a cassette printer or permanent ink; line 1 = Case ID + sample‑type abbreviation; line 2 = fixative used (add “FX” on cryomold label for fixed‑frozen tissue). Apply labels to the bottom of cryomolds and to dishes/foils.

steps.title: Record processing data
steps.instruction: Record tissue‑handling data on the Case Worksheet, including case ID, date received, shipment anomalies, processing start/end times, staff, tissues received, aliquot types/numbers, measurements, and quality notes; capture photos of harvests.

steps.title: Collect and flash‑freeze QC node
steps.instruction: Using sterile instruments, collect one lymph node ≈5 mm, place in an RNase‑free 1.5 mL cryotube, flash freeze in liquid nitrogen, and store at –80 °C for quality‑control analysis.

steps.title: Dissect nodes in cold PBS
steps.instruction: Dissect individual LNs away from fat, place each in a single well of a 24‑well cluster dish containing ice‑cold 1X D‑PBS (volume sufficient to fully cover nodes) until all nodes are collected; collect a minimum of twelve nodes (or pieces).

steps.title: Clean, measure, bisect if needed
steps.instruction: Remove residual fat/connective tissue, measure circumference on the dissection board grid, record size, and photograph; bisect any node larger than 7 mm if needed.

steps.title: Assign nodes to applications
steps.instruction: Assign each lymph node to its intended fixation/application (paraffin, fixed‑frozen OCT, fresh‑frozen OCT, CLARITY, 10×) and record the assignment on the worksheet.

steps.title: Prepare paraffin‑embedding cassettes
steps.instruction: Using two medium LNs or three small LNs, place tissue into three cassettes (max area 1 cm × 1 cm); place two cassettes in neutral buffered formalin (NBF) and one cassette in 4 % PFA, adding ≥20 mL fixative per cassette; after 20–24 h move NBF cassettes to 70 % ethanol and process within 3 days for Imaging Mass Cytometry and CODEX.

steps.title: Fix tissue for fixed‑frozen OCT
steps.instruction: Using one to two medium LNs or three small LNs, place tissue in a labeled cassette, submerge in 4 % PFA with ≥20 mL fixative; then follow the SOP at https://dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.basniede for processing and embedding.

steps.title: Create fresh‑frozen OCT block
steps.instruction: Using one medium LN or several small LNs, blot excess moisture with a clean kimwipe or gauze, submerge tissue in OCT within a labeled cryomold, then follow the SOP at https://dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bcwsixee for processing and embedding; hold and transport the block on dry ice.

steps.title: Prepare CLARITY samples
steps.instruction: Place three LNs into labeled cassettes, immerse in 4 % PFA using a fixative‑to‑tissue volume ratio of at least 20:1, fix for 20–24 h at room temperature with gentle agitation; thereafter transfer tissue to hydrogel solution and incubate 5 days at 4 °C on a rocking platform.

steps.title: Prepare samples for 10× analysis
steps.instruction: Obtain three LNs; if ≥8 mm, mince into ~5 mm × 5 mm pieces, transfer each LN (or pieces) into a 50 mL tube containing 25 mL complete DMEM/F12 media, and store at 4 °C until release or further isolation.

steps.title: Document collaboration protocols
steps.instruction: If tissue is designated for collaboration projects, indicate “Protocol B” on the worksheet and perform the specific protocols supplied by the requesting laboratory.
